name: users/__init__.py
summary: Package initializer for the users application module, marking the directory as a Python package and optionally defining its public interface.
purpose: Establishes the users directory as an importable Python package within the backend application structure, enabling modular organization of user-related domain logic and controlling package-level initialization.
responsibilities: Marks the users directory as a Python package
Defines the public API surface via __all__ exports when applicable
Executes package-level initialization logic (e.g., signal registration, app config)
Prevents circular import issues by managing cross-module dependencies at package boundary
inputs: Module imports from submodules or framework app configurations
outputs: Package namespace for the users module
architecture_notes: Serves as the package boundary for the users bounded context in a layered backend architecture (likely Django/FastAPI). Should remain lightweight; heavy initialization logic should be delegated to dedicated config or apps.py modules to avoid import side-effects. If following Django patterns, this file may be complemented by an apps.py for application configuration.
improvements: Add an explicit __all__ declaration to control the public interface if submodules are imported here
Move any complex initialization logic (e.g., signal imports, app config) to a dedicated apps.py or config module to keep the package root clean
Ensure the file is not empty (even a docstring) to clarify intent for future maintainers
Avoid importing heavy dependencies at the package root to prevent circular imports and slow startup times
